claims.text: The target HEA contains at least five elements, each at no less than 5 at.%.
Increasing Ti while substituting Nb and/or Ta changes the alloy's average valence electron concentration.
Increasing the Ti fraction enhances lattice distortion because of increased atomic-size mismatch.
Increasing the Ti fraction can induce short-range chemical ordering.
Changing the average valence electron concentration shifts the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Lattice strain caused by atomic-size differences enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Electron-phonon coupling provides conventional superconducting pairing in this class of HEAs.
Valence electron count can govern or correlate with Tc in Ta-Nb-based HEA superconductors.
Ti enrichment will raise Tc relative to a Nb-Ta-dominated baseline.
Ti enrichment will modify the upper critical field Hc2 relative to the baseline.
Reported type-A, Nb-Ta-rich HEA superconductors typically have Tc values in approximately the 4-9 K range.
Nb-Ta-rich, bcc HEA superconductors are among the most widely studied HEA superconductors.
Binary Nb-Ti alloys have better superconducting properties than binary Nb-Ta alloys.
Titanium-rich ternary Nb-Ti-Hf and Nb-Ti-Ta alloys and quaternary Nb-Ti-Ta-Hf alloys have exhibited the highest Hc2 values within their respective reported composition families.
Strong compositional disorder can be associated with superconductivity in bcc Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti solid solutions.
The predicted Ti-induced enhancement applies only while the alloy remains a homogeneous, single-phase disordered solid solution.
Phase separation or ordering caused by excessive Ti may prevent enhancement of superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The starting material is called equiatomic while also being described as Nb-Ta-dominated. An equiatomic multicomponent alloy does not give Nb or Ta preferential individual abundance, so the intended meaning of a Nb-Ta-dominated matrix is unclear.

The Hc2 change is described only as potential and uncertain, but the falsification rule can reject the hypothesis when no measurable Hc2 shift occurs. This treats an optional prediction as a required outcome.

Phase-separated or ordered samples are declared outside the boundary where the enhancement is expected, yet a correlation of property changes with phase separation or ordering is said to falsify the hypothesis. Such samples would ordinarily invalidate the test rather than decisively falsify the within-boundary claim.
